Subject: Intro + scheduling SE technical demo for Acme Retail

Hi Samir / Aisha,

Thanks for taking the time last week to chat. We think a focused technical demo with our Solutions Engineering team would be the best next step to validate latency/cost expectations and integration patterns for the Acme Retail use case.

Proposed scope (30-45 / 60 min depending on depth):
- 10 min quick product level recap (AE)
- 30 min SE deep-dive: architecture, streaming, KV caching, quantization profiles
- 15 min Q&A and next steps (procurement/security if needed)

Please share 2x 1-hour windows that work for your engineering and security teams next week. I'll loop in our SE and security leads.

Attached: acme-demo-agenda.pdf (high-level agenda).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Samir — perfect. Looping in Jordan (SE) and Vivek (security) and Rachel (procurement) so we have the right folks on the invite. Jordan, Vivek — Samir suggested Tue 5/17 10am PT or Wed 5/18 2pm PT. Any preference on your side?

Samir — for the SE prep Jordan typically asks for:
- A sample request/payload (anonymized) or a few example prompts
- Expected sequence lengths / peak concurrent requests
- Any special networking constraints (egress IPs, on-prem VPC peering)

I've attached a short SE prep checklist (se-prep-questions.docx) — can you confirm the items you can share before the demo? If there's anything sensitive, Vivek can coordinate secure transfer and we can agree on redaction.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + scheduling SE technical demo for Acme Retail

Hi all — thanks for the context. I can do either slot but prefer Wed 5/18 14:00 PT as it gives me a bit more time to pull a short demo with your sample payloads. For the demo we typically show:
- Live model behavior on a representative prompt set
- Latency profiles (cold vs warm) and caching behavior
- Options for quantized runtimes and estimated cost implications per token

Samir, if you can share an anonymized sample payload and a note about expected qps and sequence lengths that would be ideal. For networking, if you can confirm whether a test VM with outbound internet is acceptable or if we should plan for private peering that would help.

Marissa — I can also present a short slide on integration hooks.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
